Article Title: Trade & connectivity in focus: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO meet in Tajikistan
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20 to represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of Government.According to news agency ANI, citing the Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states in trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges. The participating countries are also expected to review ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions related to the organisation’s financial and institutional functioning.The agenda is expected to cover trade and investment cooperation, transport and logistics, industrial cooperation, the creative and digital economy, innovation and financial interaction, according to Interfax, which cited the Russian trade mission in Tajikistan. Social and cultural-humanitarian cooperation is also expected to feature in the discussions.India has highlighted the need to expand intra-SCO trade, lower trade costs, strengthen supply chains and improve connectivity.At a meeting of SCO ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities in Dushanbe in September, India called for simplified customs procedures, paperless trade, electronic document exchange and stronger multimodal connectivity, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.India also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in agriculture, critical minerals, pharmaceuticals, manufacturing, electronics, energy security, renewable energy and green hydrogen. It called for greater use of digital and cross-border payments and improved access to trade finance for micro, small and medium enterprises and start-ups.The October meeting will provide India an opportunity to exchange views with other SCO member states on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation. India remains actively engaged in SCO mechanisms and contributes to regional cooperation through initiatives in start-ups and innovation, digital public infrastructure and people-to-people exchanges, the Ministry of Defence said.The Council of Heads of Government adopts the SCO’s budget and addresses key issues related to cooperation within the organisation, particularly in the economic sphere. The body meets annually and is distinct from the Council of Heads of State, which serves as the organisation’s highest decision-making forum.The previous meeting of the Council of Heads of Government was held in Moscow on November 18, 2025, where India was represented by external affairs minister S Jaishankar, according to ANI.
Article Summary: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20. He will represent India at the 25th meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation’s (SCO) Council of Heads of Government. The meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO member states.

Article Title: AI cuts job demand in exposed occupations by nearly 10% across Asia: IMF report
Article Text:
As Job Placements Near, India Inc Taps Old IITs for AI Roles

AI creates demand for new skills

India faces jobs and skills challenge

Education, reskilling key to managing AI disruption

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia, with employer demand falling by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022, according to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) October 2026 Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific.The report, based on approximately 40 million online job postings across 19 Asian economies, highlights the challenges facing countries such as India, Indonesia and the Philippines as they seek to create productive jobs for growing working-age populations while AI transforms the sectors expected to absorb new workers.However, the decline in demand for workers in AI-exposed occupations appears to have stabilised, suggesting that the technology’s impact on employment is not limited to job displacement.The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation and AI agent development.Employers are increasingly seeking workers who can integrate AI into business processes, improve productivity and translate technological capabilities into practical applications.Firm-level adoption of AI, however, remains uneven. Around 6% of firms in Asia explicitly seek AI skills in their job postings, the report said.Businesses adopting AI are experiencing stronger labour demand growth than those that have not adopted the technology, including in occupations highly exposed to automation. This suggests that AI can complement human capabilities even as it reduces demand for certain tasks.The implications of AI differ across Asian economies. Emerging economies such as India may initially be less exposed to the technology because a large share of their workforce remains employed in agriculture and other sectors less affected by AI.However, this could pose a longer-term challenge if AI makes it harder for workers to transition into higher-productivity manufacturing and services, the report said.For countries with expanding working-age populations, the challenge is to generate enough productive employment while ensuring that workers have the skills required by an increasingly technology-driven economy.The report emphasises that the response to AI must go beyond encouraging technological adoption. Education reform, reskilling programmes, digital infrastructure and stronger labour-market institutions will be essential to prepare workers for changing occupational demands.Businesses will also need to invest in workforce development alongside AI adoption to help employees adapt to new roles and changing skill requirements.The report suggests that AI need not become a barrier to inclusive growth. With timely investments in skills and preparedness, Asian economies could use the technology to boost productivity, encourage innovation and support sustainable employment.
Article Summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping labour demand across Asia. Employer demand has fallen by nearly 10% in occupations more exposed to the technology since the launch of ChatGPT in November 2022. The IMF report points to the emergence of new employment opportunities requiring specialised AI skills.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday visited Calcutta Medical College and Hospital, where people injured in the stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata are undergoing treatment.At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in the stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening, following a surge in the crowd amid rain.Kolkata Police have registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the incident, an officer said. Police are also working to identify those killed in the stampede.Shah had earlier expressed condolences to the families of the deceased, describing the incident as “extremely distressing”. He also said he had spoken to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari to take stock of the situation.Following the tragedy, Kolkata Police imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, in parts of the city for three days, from October 18 to October 20, to maintain law and order.According to an order issued by Kolkata Police Commissioner Ajay Nand, the restrictions cover areas under the jurisdiction of Bowbazar police station, bounded by College Street, Central Avenue (CR Avenue), Colootola Street and Eden Hospital Road.The order prohibits unlawful assemblies of five or more people, carrying lathis or other lethal and dangerous weapons, and any activity likely to disturb public tranquillity or cause a breach of peace in the designated area.The order states: "Now, therefore, in exercise of the power conferred by Sub-Section (1) of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 read with the Sub-Section (3) of the said Section, I, Ajay Nand, Commissioner of Police, Kolkata being an Executive Magistrate for the Metropolitan area of Kolkata as well as in the district of South 24 Parganas(within the limits of the suburbs of Kolkata falling under Kolkata police jurisdiction) do hereby prohibit for a period of 03(three) days from 18.10.2026 to 20.10.2026 or until further order, any unlawful assembly of 05(five) or more persons, carrying of lathi, any lethal or other dangerous weapons or doing of any act which is likely to cause breach of the peace and disturbances of the public tranquility within the said Area in the town of Kolkata. "The restrictions were imposed amid concerns that demonstrations, rallies and meetings could lead to violence and affect public safety. They will remain in force until October 20 or until further orders.

Article Title: FSSAI may curb sugar in baby food, set pesticide caps for tea
Article Text:
The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16 (AI image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has proposed two changes to food safety rules: prohibiting the addition of sucrose and fructose to products meant for babies up to six months and setting maximum residue limits for two pesticides in tea.The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. Sucrose and fructose can be added when needed, but their combined amount cannot exceed 20% of total carbohydrates. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months.The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity and related health risks. It also complements recommendations for exclusive breastfeeding during the first six months. A doctor said the restriction must be enforced at the licensing stage. “FSSAI should also consider extending the ban to products intended for children above six months, given concerns over obesity.FSSAI has also proposed maximum residue limits of 20 parts per million (ppm) for acetamiprid and 50 ppm for imidacloprid in tea.Maxim­um residue limits specify the highest legally permitted co­n­­centration of pesticide residues in food and provide ben­chmarks. They do not indicate the amount necessarily pr­esent in a particular sample.One doctor said the proposed limits need to be accompanied by realistic assessments of consumer exposure. “Since tea is consumed several times a day, it is important to assess how much of these chemicals passes from the leaves into the brewed drink.”
Article Summary: The draft amendments were published in the Gazette of India on Oct 16. Currently, lactose and glucose polymers are the preferred carbohydrate sources in infant foods. The proposed amendment seeks to prohibit their addition in products for babies up to six months. The proposal aims to limit early exposure to added sugars amid concerns over childhood obesity.

Indian Captain Smit Machchhar, who survived an assault by his Omani co-pilot aboard a flydubai flight in September, recalled the ordeal and how he might not survive.In a teaser released by Sky News Arabia ahead of an exclusive interview, asked whether there was a moment when he thought he might not make it, Machchhar said he told himself he needed to act before it was too late. "I mean, I'm trying to get over it now, but yes, there was a moment that I realised, and I told myself that, Smith, do something. "I remember being face down, and of course the panic which was there, the screaming which was there," he said.He also praised the colleague who took over the controls during the crisis, calling the colleague's actions commendable. "It's something that I'll keep with me till I die," Machchhar said.The interview comes weeks after the September 30 incident aboard flydubai flight FZ1073, which was travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The Indian captain was allegedly attacked by his Omani co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, inside the cockpit.Despite his injuries, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, allowing passengers to intervene and overpower the alleged attacker. The aircraft experienced a sharp drop in altitude before it was brought under control and diverted to Tabuk in Saudi Arabia, where it landed safely.The full interview is scheduled to air on Sky News Arabia at 9 pm Abu Dhabi time or 10.30pm IST (5 pm GMT).

At an event in Chhattisgarh to distribute assistive devices to victims maimed in Naxal attacks, he accused Congress of failing to provide basic amenities for decades.Addressing the event via video conferencing, Shah said the programme, organised under 'seva sankalp abhiyan' to mark 25 years of PM Modi's 'seva and samarpan' (service), would help tribal people who had lost limbs or sensory abilities due to Naxal violence. Article Title: A 7am email to employer, ‘I love you’ on clothes and a chilling ‘leaving this world’ note on wife’s birthday: What preceded Malayali techie couple’s deaths in Gurgaon flat
Article Text:
An IT professional, Mohammad Aslam, and his wife, Farhana, were discovered dead in their Gurgaon apartment.

Moved to Gurgaon three months ago

Email prompted colleagues to contact landlord





GURGAON: An email sent to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world”, set off a chain of events that led to the discovery of an IT professional and his wife dead in their Gurgaon apartment on Wednesday.The techie had also shared the phone numbers of his parents and landlord, asking the company to inform them.When the landlord reached the flat in Tower 7 of M3M Marina, he found Mohammad Aslam (30) hanging and his wife, Farhana, who was about to turn 28, lying on the floor with an injury mark on her neck. He alerted Badshapur police station.Inside the flat, police found a note bearing the words “We are leaving this world”. The words “I love you” had also been scribbled on Farhana's clothes. Investigators are examining the messages and other material recovered from the apartment as they piece together what led to the couple’s deaths.Police suspect Aslam killed Farhana before dying by suicide, but said the sequence of events and the cause of death had not yet been established. A murder case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The couple’s families, based in Kerala, have been left struggling to understand what happened. Relatives said they knew of no marital discord and described the couple as being close to each other. They said Aslam had been undergoing treatment for depression for around a year and a half.“The couple shared a really close bond. Both were happy with each other and had no marital discord. There was no issue with the family either. But hearing this has left both families in shock,” said Faisal, Farhana’s brother.The couple had relocated to Gurgaon from Bengaluru around three months ago. Aslam, a native of Kozhikode, had joined an Indonesia-based IT company with an office in Sector 58. Farhana, who hailed from Malappuram, worked from home for an IT firm based in Bengaluru.They married in 2023 and spent around two years in Bengaluru before moving to Gurgaon.Aslam graduated in electrical and electronics engineering from NIT Calicut in 2018 and completed his MBA from IIM Indore in 2020. Farhana had completed her BTech from MES College of Engineering in Kuttippuram, Kerala.Family members said Aslam had been taking medication and undergoing therapy for depression for around 18 months. They said neither he nor Farhana had discussed any problems that might have suggested they were going through a difficult period.Faisal said relatives suspected work pressure could have contributed to the tragedy, although they had no confirmation of what the couple had been experiencing.“We used to go on trips together, and I connected very well with my brother-in-law. We suspect that work pressure in the IT sector may have led to the incident. They never discussed anything that suggested they were suffering or going through something so bad. Work pressure is the only reason we suspect, but only God and the two of them knew what was happening,” he said.Another relative, Abdul Azeez, said the family believed the incident may have occurred around midnight on Wednesday. Farhana was due to celebrate her birthday that day.“Her parents have been left shattered. We just want to take their bodies home,” he said.After Aslam’s email arrived around 7am on Wednesday, his colleagues contacted the landlord using the details provided. The landlord went to the apartment, found the couple dead and alerted the police.An emergency response vehicle reached the spot around 8am, followed by a larger police team. An officer said the flat’s door was not bolted.Police recovered three laptops, two mobile phones, a rope, the note, a diary, scissors and a pen drive from the apartment. The electronic devices were seized for forensic analysis. Police said the note contained no allegations against anyone.Both bodies were shifted to a mortuary and identified by family members on Friday. Autopsies were yet to be conducted.“The cause of death will be established only after the autopsy report. It is suspected that the husband killed his wife and later died by suicide after sending an email to his office,” the officer said.Police are examining the evidence to establish the circumstances and sequence of the deaths.
Article Summary: Mohammad Aslam, 30, and his wife, Farhana, 28, were found dead in their Gurgaon apartment. Police suspect Aslam killed his wife before committing suicide. Aslam sent an email to his employer at around 7am, saying “we are leaving this world’

NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a government job for the family of each person killed in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata.The state government will also bear the entire cost of medical treatment for the injured and provide Rs 5 lakh to each of them, Adhikari said, adding that a fact-finding committee would be constituted to investigate the incident."This is a tragic incident. 19 people have lost their lives, 17 of whom died on the spot... 25 people have been injured; 24 of them are out of danger, while one remains in critical condition," the chief minister said. He added that the government was making every possible effort to assist the affected families and that he had personally met relatives of the deceased.Adhikari said the state government would seek the intervention of the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to constitute a fact-finding committee, which would include special task force (STF) and forensic teams. The investigation would examine the circumstances leading to the stampede and identify those responsible for the crowd management arrangements.Kolkata Police's Anti-Rowdy Section (ARS) has collected CCTV footage from the site, which will be examined as part of the investigation."We will check the footage and take appropriate measures against those who failed to manage the crowd. That could be a member of the puja committee, a homeguard, a temporary worker, a policeman, or a private company security guard. Nobody will be spared," Adhikari said.He said the state government was making arrangements for postmortems in accordance with the law and that six of the deceased had been identified so far. Officials were also coordinating with the families of the victims.The chief minister said the families who had met him had expressed faith in the state government. He added that the Prime Minister's Office had sought a report from the chief secretary, which had been submitted, and that the Centre and the state were working together to provide assistance.Adhikari also criticised the previous state government over its handling of past tragedies, accusing some people of attempting to politicise the current incident."Everyone is well aware of the role of the previous government in similar incidents that occurred in the past. At least 19 people died and 25 were injured after a crowd surge amid rain, according to officials.A police officer said people waiting outside the pandal rushed forward as it began raining, causing some to fall on the road and triggering the stampede. Adhikari said an announcement made by the organisers of the community Durga Puja had led to a rush among revellers, resulting in what he described as a "painful incident".Officials of the organising club, private security guards and personnel on duty were detained for questioning, he said. Article Title: 'Do something. You can’t die like this': flydubai pilot Capt Smit Machchar recounts cockpit attack
Article Text:
'It went on like a normal day till it wasn’t,' Smit recalled

MUMBAI: Two hours into the flight from Dubai to Tel Avivi, flydubai commander, Capt Smit Machchar was checking landing time and fuel figures on the computer when something struck hard at the back of his head. He thought part of his Boeing 737’s cockpit roof had broken loose. Seconds later, as more blows rained in, he turned and saw it was his co-pilot. Bleeding, his vision shrunk to a few inches, he drifted in and out of consciousness during those fateful minutes when the aircraft went into a rapid descent, while the attack continued. “There was a moment I told myself, Smit, do something, you can’t die like this,” said the flydubai pilot, recounting the Sept 30 terror attack on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv, which was diverted and landed in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. In his first extended account since the incident, given to Sky News Arabia on Sat evening, Machchar said an ordinary flight, with a co-pilot he was flying with for the first time, turned violent minutes after the man stood up to pray.It was a route he had flown many times. An augmented crew was on board, and the relief captain was to take over operating duties after landing.“Normal flight,” he told the channel. “It went on like a normal day till it wasn’t.”About two hours in, the relief captain had dropped by the cockpit to chat about rosters and flying hours when the co-pilot, who had stepped out for a toilet break, returned. A few minutes into their conversation, he said he wished to pray and asked the relief captain to step out. Machchar said such requests are accepted in the region when the flight is stable.The co-pilot asked the other Captain to step out, stood up behind him and began praying. “Out of respect, I did not look back. I was checking the landing time and fuel figures on the computer, the routine background tasks of the monitoring pilot. Suddenly there was a very hard hit at the back of my head,” he said. “It was something very strong and hard. I didn’t know at that point what had hit me.” He fell forward, and his mind reached for training. “My first thought was, okay, something has broken from the aircraft roof, and it has been a catastrophic damage. I was planning to regain my composure and check my systems.”The blows kept coming. Within seconds his vision had narrowed to a few inches, he said. When he glanced back, he understood. “He was saying something while hitting me, but I could not understand.” Machchar unbuckled and tried to shield himself, taking a blow on his hand. “That’s when something flipped,” he said. He screamed for the relief captain and, since the door switch was within reach, managed to open it. He lost consciousness for the first time soon after. He recalled hearing shouting between the co-pilot and the other crew before the door shut again, with the co-pilot threatening to hit them too.It was after this, he said, that he heard the engines spool down and felt the aircraft pitch into a dive. “I don’t have to see the instruments, I can have my eyes closed and still know the engines are spooling down and the aircraft is going down. Every pilot will tell you this.”Drifting in and out of consciousness from blood loss, he said, he reached a point of decision. “I told myself, Smit, do something. You can’t die like this. I’m not saying I accepted my death. It was like, do something, otherwise...” The pilot added his memory of what followed is fragmentary, a gap he is still working through with doctors and psychologists. He said he remembers locking his legs against something and pushing toward the door. He said he remembers then lying face down between the cockpit and the galley, the door open, passengers panicking.Machchar credited his colleague for taking the controls and recovering the aircraft, calling it something he will carry “till I die.” Asked about the speculation over how the plane was saved, he declined to single anyone out.“Everyone did the best in their capacity,” he said, including crew and passengers.He said he knew he was out of danger only when the aircraft touched down. Until then a doctor on board and his crew kept him conscious. “At that point, what I was more focused on was to not give up on life. You say you see flashes and stuff like that (speaking about death). You just remember the person who matters the most,” he said. The first call he made was to his 2-year old son. In the days that followed the incident, he continued to get flashes of the first blow. The commander added that he has been getting better with each passing day and can now sit and have conversations.
Article Summary: Capt Smit Machchar was on flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. Two hours into the flight he was hit hard at the back of his head. He thought part of his Boeing 737’s cockpit roof had broken loose. The pilot said his memory of what followed is fragmented.

Article Title: 'Nine murders' claim, then a clarification: How 'Chhote Sarkar' has put Nitish, JD(U) on the spot
Article Text:

In 2004, Anant Singh weighed Nitish Kumar against silver coins during a public rally in the Barh parliamentary constituency to show his support.

Fate tied to bahubali brother

Pet lover who loves python

Anant Singh with his horses

NEW DELHI: Anant Singh , Bihar's bahubali MLA, who is intensely popular on social media reels for his impromptu one liners in local Magahi dialect, made a jittering claim to prove his loyality and sacrifice for JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar "I got nine people murdered," he said on camera, reviving the distressing memory of Jungle Raj that once besieged Bihar. The statement also had a dramatic irony as he was mentioning the man who ruled Bihar as 'Sushasan Babu', Nitish Kumar.Speaking to reporters about his years of loyalty with Bihar's former chief minister Nitish Kumar, the six-time legislator said: “Who has made so many sacrifices as I have? Nitish Kumar was nothing back then; he used to roam around here and there. At that time, while being with Nitish Kumar, I got nine people murdered.”However, maybe after releasing the political gravity of his remark, the Mokama MLA backtracked and pinned the blame on Lalu Yadav, who was once an ally of Nitish Kumar.The video went viral and the timing was fatal, because Singh, popular as 'Chhote Sarkar', is already at odds with his party over the Patna Graduates’ MLC election.He is backing the candidate fielded by Prashant Kishor against JD(U)’s Neeraj Kumar, the very man he defeated in the 2015 assembly election.As criticism came crashing in from the party and the opposition, Singh sensed the backlash and tweaked his remark, saying: “During the Lalu Prasad regime, nine of my associates were killed, and I myself was shot. It was because we aligned ourselves with Nitish Kumar that Lalu had them killed. We have suffered such immense losses. My father also passed away due to a heart attack.”However, the RJD held back the attack as Lalu's party spokesperson Shakti Singh Yadav, said: “Anant has publicly confessed to killing nine persons during the NDA regime. Now Nitish will have to offer explanations.”He went further: “Although he (Anant) has confessed to his involvement in nine murders, the responsibility straightaway goes to Nitish regime...Is paap se chhutkara nahin milekga (There will be no escape from this sin).”Anant Singh is no ordinary legislator as locals rarely use his given name. They call him 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s.His story begins with his elder brother, Dilip Singh. Dilip won as an independent and became a minister in Lalu Prasad’s cabinet during its first term, from 1990 to 1995. Dilip Singh is remembered as the first of the so-called bahubalis, or musclemen politicians, to reach such a post.Anant Singh, who first handled his brother’s election campaigns, took over the family's political reins following Dilip Singh's electoral defeat to rival strongman Surajbhan Singh in 2000.In the next election cycle in 2005, Nitish Kumar, who came to power that year promising to clean up one of India’s poorest and most fractured states, brought Anant Singh into the JD(U). Anant Singh's backing could help the party among upper castes, who did not naturally support Nitish Kumar.However, his allegiance to Nitish began a year before. In 2004, Anant Singh weighed Nitish Kumar against silver coins during a public rally in the Barh parliamentary constituency to show his support.Anant Singh successfully contested the Mokama assembly seat in 2005 on a JD(U) ticket.Once asked why he had embraced a man with such a reputation, Nitish Kumar replied, “There are certain compulsions of politics.”Anant Singh then again contested as a JD(U) candidate in 2010, and the relationship lasted until he quit the party before the 2015 polls.Anant Singh keeps a python as a pet, owns an elephant trained to shake hands and rides an antique buggy pulled by expensive horses.Residents describe him holding a durbar where he settles disputes, hears complaints against the police and acts against “miscreants”. Admirers credit him with safer streets and quicker access to services. Critics see a parallel government.Aanant Singh has faced around two dozen serious cases, ranging from murder and kidnapping to conspiracy to kill and the possession of illegal arms. But for years none ended in a conviction, as judges died, officers were transferred and evidence went missing.In his last affidavit he filed in 2025 Bihar elections, he mentioned 28 criminal cases involving undue influence or personation at an election, making preparation to commit dacoity, insult intended to provoke breach of the peace, rioting and armed with a deadly weapon, dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person.In 2015, after he was arrested on murder and kidnapping charges, Nitish Kumar cut him loose. The move was widely read as a gesture to Lalu Prasad Yadav , his old rival turned new partner. Nitish JD(U) had snapped ties with the BJP-led NDA over Narendra Modi being chosen as the PM face.Anant Singh, however, fought the election from jail as an independent. His wife, Neelam, campaigned in his name and called him a “rare diamond”. Interestingly, he won comfortably without stepping onto the campaign trail.The pressure returned in 2019 after police arrested three suspected sharpshooters on 15 July, who allegedly planned to kill a contractor, Bhola Singh, and his brother Mukesh Singh.They reportedly told investigators that Anant Singh had given them the contract. He gave a voice sample to the state forensic science laboratory.Soon afterwards, an AK-47 and hand grenades were recovered from his ancestral house, and he was booked under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, or UAPA. Anant Singh disappeared for nearly a week.“The man, whose name once spelt terror, is now running for cover,” a senior IPS officer said at the time. He eventually surrendered in a Delhi court and alleged a “conspiracy by political forces”, an apparent dig at the JD(U).Nonetheless, Bihar politics is never bereft of bahubalis. And 2020 was different from 2015. Nitish was back with NDA with ever-dominant BJP under Prime Minister Narendra Modi. And RJD, which was by then handled actively by Lalu's son Tejashwi Yadav, forged an alliance with the Congress.This dynamic also shifted the allegiance of Anant Singh, who fought on RJD's ticket and Nitish Kumar's party. Still in jail in 2020, he won with 78,721 votes, about 53 per cent of valid votes cast, by a margin of more than 65,000.In 2021, a special court in Patna sentenced him to 10 years in the arms case, which cost him his seat. Neelam Devi then won the by-election for the RJD, showing that the family’s hold on Mokama had not loosened.Nitish again dumped the BJP in 2022 and returned to the RJD's Mahagathbandhan fold. But nothing much changed for Anant Singh.In February 2024, Nitish Kumar flipped again, leaving the RJD-led alliance for the BJP-led NDA. He won the floor test comfortably with 129 votes, as the opposition walked out. Anant Singh’s wife, Neelam Devi, was one of three RJD MLAs who cross-voted in his favour, a pointed gesture even though the numbers did not depend on it.Months later, Anant Singh stepped out of Patna jail on 15 days of parole in the middle of the Lok Sabha elections. He backed Lalan Singh of the JD(U) in Munger, a sworn enemy whom his wife had challenged on a Congress ticket in 2019. Munger has roughly 3.5 lakh Bhumihar voters, the community to which Singh belongs. The RJD questioned the timing of his release.The most dramatic chapter came during the Mokama assembly contest in 2025. Dularchand Yadav, 76, was murdered while campaigning for a Jan Suraaj candidate. Police arrested Singh, then the JD(U) nominee, in connection with the killing. The NDA responded that, unlike under the Lalu regime, no leader enjoys immunity from legal action.The case revived an old rivalry with Surajbhan Singh, another Bhumihar strongman. Surajbhan began in the LJP, later moved close to the RJD, and saw his own electoral influence shrink after criminal convictions. His wife, Veena Devi, kept the family relevant in nearby seats. The two men have long competed for land, contracts and political dominance.The arithmetic made the stakes plain. Mokama has about 2.9 lakh voters. Bhumihars number roughly 55,000 to 60,000, Dhanuks about 45,000 and Yadavs about 40,000.Muslims and Dalits together make up roughly 30 per cent. A shift of 5 to 10 per cent could move 15,000 to 25,000 votes. The killing of a Yadav campaigner threatened to unsettle backward caste voters, while the Bhumihar vote risked splitting between two powerful figures.Net-net, contrary to Anant Singh' remark, "Chhote Sarkar" has been an ally, an outcast, a prisoner, a convict and a kingmaker, often within a few years. And this time again, he has been vocal against his party's MLC candidate Neeraj Kumar and backing Jan Suraaj's Anuj Kumar Singh.“Nishant (Nitish Kumar's son) should not have campaigned for Neeraj Kumar. Sometimes he is taken to Barh, sometimes some other places, but there are few people to support him,” Anant Singh said, claiming he would “medically treat” Neeraj in the election.
Article Summary: Anant Singh, Bihar's bahubali MLA, made a jittering claim to prove his loyality and sacrifice for JD(U) chief Nitish Kumar. Singh is popular as 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s.

NEW DELHI: At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured after a stampede-like incident at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening, as heavy rain and a sudden rush of visitors triggered chaos near the exit gate. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee expressed grief over the incident.The incident took place at around 7:40 pm at the Sarada Park (Chorbagan) Durga Puja pandal, where a surge of visitors near the exit gate reportedly triggered panic as rain continued to fall.Kolkata Police said all the injured had been rescued and taken to the hospital. In a post on X, the Prime Minister’s Office said: “The stampede in Kolkata is extremely distressing. My thoughts are with those who have lost their loved ones. May the injured recover at the earliest. The local administration is providing all possible assistance to those affected.”The PMO also wrote, "The Prime Minister has announced that each relative of those who lost their lives in the stampede in Kolkata will be provided with a one-time financial assistance of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF).Each of the injured will be given financial assistance of 50,000 rupees.The Prime Minister has announced that each relative of those who lost their lives in the stampede in Kolkata will be provided with a one-time financial assistance of 2 lakh rupees from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF). She extended her condolences to the bereaved families and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured.Union home minister Amit Shah also expressed anguish over the incident and said he had spoken with West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari.HM Shah wrote in a post on X, “I pray for the peace of the souls of those who have lost their lives in this tragic accident and extend my deepest condolences to the bereaved family members. He also urged Congress workers to provide all possible assistance in relief efforts.Meanwhile, Governor RN Ravi also expressed his grief in a statement issued by Lok Bhavan. “I am deeply heartbroken by the tragic stampede incident at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, resulting in the loss of many precious lives. In this hour of grief, I extend my heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. I pray for the swift recovery of the injured.”Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and chief secretary Manoj Agarwal visited the hospital, while health minister Saradwat Mukherjee and other senior officials also reached the hospital to check on the injured.West Bengal minister Nisith Pramanik wrote, "Deeply saddened by the pandal collapse in Chorbagan. Article Title: 'He kept on hitting': Indian flydubai pilot Smit Machchhar reveals what happened mid-flight as he was stabbed
Article Text:
Smit Machchhar is recovering in Abu Dhabi

‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this’

‘Everyone did their best’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your biggest takeaway from Captain Smit Machchhar's experience? The importance of quick thinking The need for teamwork Survival instincts are crucial 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Indian pilot Smit Machchhar who was attacked by his co-pilot aboard a Flydubai flight has recalled how a routine journey turned into a fight for survival, describing the repeated blows to his head, his attempts to call for help and the moments he lost consciousness as the aircraft went into a dive.after he was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane.In an exclusive 1st news interview after being stabbed, with Sky News Arabia, Captain Smith Machchhar said there had been nothing unusual about the flight until about two hours after take-off. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.Giving out details as he remembered he said, "when I was just in in the checking my computer for the timing and everything, uh suddenly there was a a very hard hit at the back of my head, right here. And uh it was quite hard and felt that it was something which was very strong."He said he initially thought something had broken off the aircraft's roof and hit him, causing catastrophic damage. Drawing on his training, he tried to regain his composure and check the aircraft's systems. “My thought process went on that track, that oh, there is a big damage in the aircraft which has hit me at the back,” he said.But within seconds, he realised he was being attacked. “He kept on hitting,” Machchhar said.He recalled turning around and realising what was happening, although the impact had severely restricted his field of vision.“Immediately, I would say in the next few seconds, my vision was restricted to like few inches,” he said, adding that he learnt about the extent of the impact from doctors later.His first response was to protect himself from further blows. He quickly unbuckled his seatbelt, turned around and tried to block the attack, sustaining an injury to his hand. “At this point, it was very obvious what was going on,” he said.Machchhar said he immediately tried to get help from another captain who was on board and was expected to operate the return flight. “I was screaming his name and I was trying because the switch was very close to me to open the door. I was trying to just get help in,” he said.He lost consciousness amid the commotion but remembered managing to open the cockpit door. He could hear shouting as the other crew members confronted the co-pilot. “The door shut immediately after that because he threatened to hit them as well,” Machchhar said.By then, he was struggling to stay conscious and could feel his strength fading because of blood loss. Soon afterwards, he heard the engine sounds change and felt the aircraft go into a dive. “Since I’ve been flying for such a long time, I don’t have to see the instruments to figure out or hear the engine to know what’s happening,” he said.Machchhar said he repeatedly drifted in and out of consciousness but realised he had to fight to survive. “There was a moment where I realised and I told myself that, ‘Smith, do something. You can’t die like this,’” he said.His memories of what happened next remain fragmented. He recalled trying to reach the door, bracing his leg against something and pushing himself forward.“The next memory that I have is the door’s open and I’m lying between the cockpit and the galley,” he said. He remembered being face down as panic and shouting continued around him.While Machchhar was fighting to survive, another captain took over the controls and helped save the aircraft. “The other thing, how my other colleague who took over the controls and saved the day again is commendable. It’s something that I’ll keep with me till I die,” he said.Asked what he wanted people to understand about the incident amid speculation over how the plane was saved, Machchhar said everyone on board had done what they could.“I think everyone in world everyone in world did the best in their capacity to save the day,” he said. The pilot said the first blow continued to haunt him in the days after the attack.“Immediately after the event, I used to get flashes of the first hit. And trust me, it shook me up for the first few days,” he said, describing how the memory would return suddenly and leave his heart racing.But what stayed with him most was the determination of those on board. “One thing that I would take away from that day was the determination, the sheer determination of everyone to survive,” he said.Machchhar said he felt out of danger only when the aircraft touched down in Saudi Arabia. By then, a doctor was attending to him in the galley, while crew members worked to keep him conscious.Asked whom he thought of first, he replied: “My son.” His two-year-old son, wife and daughter live with him in the UAE.Machchhar also expressed gratitude for the medical treatment he received in Saudi Arabia and after being brought back to the UAE. “From the first day onwards, the way I was taken care of, the way I was brought back to the UAE, even the care that I was given in Saudi is something I would never forget in my life,” he said.Still recovering from the traumatic incident, he said he felt grateful for the care and support he had received over the preceding two-and-a-half weeks.“Grateful is the word I would say right now,” he said.
Article Summary: Captain Smit Machchhar was stabbed by his Omani copilot Hamam Al Hammami who was allegedly trying to crash the plane. He was carrying out routine checks in the cockpit when the attack began, initially mistaking the first blow to the back of his head for damage to the aircraft.

Article Title: ‘Taking away right to vote, protest’: Uddhav backs opposition's ‘regime change’ call against government

NEW DELHI: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Saturday backed the opposition’s call for 'regime change', saying a government that takes away people’s right to express themselves through voting and protests needs to be changed.“Police are assaulting youth and women, tearing their clothes. Such a regime needs to be buried,” he said, referring to alleged police action against protesters in the national capital.Addressing the Akhil Bharatiya Marathi Patrakar Parishad, Thackeray questioned the deployment of a large number of police personnel in Delhi during protests called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and other parties.“Have thousands of police personnel been deployed in Delhi to ‘play dandia’?” he asked.Taking a swipe at the BJP over media reports of a cockroach effigy being burnt during Dussehra celebrations, Thackeray said that those who claim to have brought Ram are scared of cockroaches.“We are here to change the regime,” he asserted.Thackeray’s remarks came amid a political row over the opposition’s protests against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The call intensified after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan called for “regime change”, arguing that spreading “disaffection” against a government was not a crime in a democracy.“This government keeps on saying this is the opposition's operation of regime change. We are only appealing to save the electoral democracy in this country. If such barbarism continues, there will definitely be a regime change. We all want a regime change. Is there anything wrong with that? Regime change is a democratic right of every citizen, and creating disaffection against the government is not an offence,” Bhushan had said at a press conference on Thursday.Dipke was granted conditional bail on Saturday and asked to sign a peace bond. He had been detained on Friday after stepping out of his home in Delhi’s Jhandewalan area to join the CJP’s “Lehra Do Tiranga” protest at Connaught Place. He was arrested the following morning for allegedly violating a peace bond furnished on October 10, PTI reported.Earlier on Saturday, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut also demanded regime change, alleging that authorities were preventing young people from waving the national flag."Can one not protest by waving the tricolour in this country? We wanted to wave the tricolour. Under the Narendra Modi, Amit Shah and Devendra Fadnavis regime, you don’t allow the youth to wave the tricolour; instead, you arrest them or even kidnap them. Which is why there is talk of regime change. And this regime change will happen,” Raut asserted.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, meanwhile, accused the opposition of seeking to topple the government outside the democratic process. In a post on X, Fadnavis questioned the opposition's stance on SIR, “Why do they oppose ‘SIR’? Because they want a ‘regime change.’”"It is precisely because they have no chance of coming to power through elections that they talk about a ‘regime change’!” he added.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray backs the opposition's call for'regime change' He says a government that takes away people's right to express themselves through voting and protests needs to be changed. His remarks come amid a political row over the opposition’s protests against alleged electoral irregularities.

Article Title: FSSAI cracks down on Priyagold biscuit maker
Article Text:
The FSSAI has taken legal action against three companies over serious violations of food safety standards

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies, sanctioning prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd, while issuing notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever (HUL) over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.Action against Surya Food & Agro followed a consumer complaint that led officials to find bran meant for cattle feed being used as a fibre source in Priyagold biscuits.The gunny bags containing the material for the biscuits were marked for cattle feed. Inspectors also flagged deficiencies in plant hygiene, pest control, raw material storage and segregation, personnel hygiene and premises maintenance. The company’s FSSAI licence was suspended following the inspection, and the competent authority has now sanctioned prosecution. Attempts to reach the company for comment were unsuccessful.FSSAI has issued notices to Nestlé India over its Nescafé ready-to-drink range, including Cappuccino, Choco Mocha and Chilled Latte, manufactured by Schreiber Dynamix Dairies and Lotus Dairy Products. The regulator flagged discrepancies between the front-of-pack description “Flavoured Milk” and the back label, which classified the products as “Proprietary Food – 1.12 Dairy Based Drink”.Online listings described them as “Coffee Flavoured Milk” and carried claims about the goodness of flavoured double-toned milk, which FSSAI said were inconsistent with the declared product category. The companies have been asked to explain why action should not be initiated under food safety laws.A separate notice to Nestlé concerned its Resource Renal vanilla flavour powder, intended for dietary management of people with conservatively treated chronic kidney disease. FSSAI said the product lacked the required prior approval and that the prescribed vegetarian or non-vegetarian symbol was missing from the label.In a statement the company said, “FSSAI has sent a communication to Nestlé India concerning the label declarations/classification of the Nescafe Ready To Drink products. This does not relate to product safety or product quality. Mentioned products are safe to consume and meet all applicable food safety requirements.We will be submitting our response to the authorities and will be engaging with them as per due process established under law. ” Hindustan Unilever was issued notices over claims on Horlicks Women’s Plus Chocolate Nutrition Drink, including “Nutrition for Strong Bones” and “Clinically Proven to Help Improve Bone Strength in 6 Months”.In a statement to the press, the company spokesperson said, “Hindustan Unilever Limited is committed to providing safe, high-quality products that comply with all applicable regulatory requirements. Horlicks Women’s Plus and Mother’s Plus has been developed based on established nutritional science and is manufactured in accordance with stringent quality and safety standards. All product communication is developed in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and governance processes. We will share all the scientific and regulatory evidence with the authorities as per normal process of review.”
Article Summary: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has stepped up enforcement against major food companies. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Priyagold biscuit maker Surya Food & Agro Ltd, Dodla Dairy Ltd and Ueir Organic Foods Pvt Ltd. It has also issued notices to Nestlé India and Hindustan Unilever over alleged labelling violations and misleading product claims.

Article Title: Crowd, rain or misleading announcement: What led to Kolkata stampede tragedy?
Article Text:
Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them

What we know about Kolkata stampede

Crowd management and security under scrutiny

State orders safety review of pandals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A sudden surge of people, heavy rain and alleged confusion over announcements and entry-exit routes are among the factors being investigated after a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening.The incident occurred around 7.15pm on Maha Saptami, when a large crowd waiting on the narrow Radha Madhab Saha Lane to enter the pandal reportedly surged forward as a downpour began. Those already inside were caught in the rush, with people unable to move towards the exit as visitors ahead blocked their way. Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them.A misleading announcement by the puja committee is also suspected to have added to the confusion, while the blowing of whistles by private security guards may have triggered a rush among visitors, according to CM Adhikari.Kolkata Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy, a senior officer told PTI. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper, leaving visitors confused during peak hours.Locals also questioned the police deployment at the venue, claiming that personnel were largely stationed near the VIP entrance."I have not seen adequate police presence this year. This resulted in the mismanagement," Chorbagan resident Sanghamitra Bhowmik told PTI.Another concern raised by locals was the alleged lack of administrative assistance in taking the injured to hospitals."There must be some lapses, but these should be probed. Whether lapses were on the part of the organisers or they had flouted the rules to erect the pandal will be checked," the police officer told PTI.A forensic team visited the site late on Saturday to collect evidence. Police are questioning the organisers and examining CCTV footage, while also seeking details of the security guards and other personnel deployed to manage the crowd. Officers who were posted at the venue will also be questioned as part of the investigation.Adhikari, who visited the injured at Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, said the incident had raised concerns about safety arrangements at crowded Durga Puja venues. According to hospital sources, 11 injured people were shifted to SSKM Hospital. The deceased included 13 women and a child, a source at the medical college said.The chief minister announced a high-level committee to inspect prominent pandals across West Bengal and review crowd management, exit routes, lighting and structural safety. The panel will be led by Disaster Management Principal Secretary Rajesh Sinha, Fire Services Director General Anuj Sharma and Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Javed Shamim.Adhikari urged organisers to follow official safety recommendations, warning against elaborate themes that compromise visitors' safety. He also called for wider exits, better lighting and the removal of bottlenecks created by temporary rope enclosures. Where complex structures obstruct movement, organisers may be advised to restrict rituals to the inner sanctum and use LED screens outside.The state government has announced Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased victim. A toll-free helpline, 18003455678, has also been set up to help people seeking information about those affected.
Article Summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening. Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper.

NEW DELHI: The promised nonstop drive between Delhi and Mumbai may have to wait until Dec 2029, with the govt’s flagship Delhi-Mumbai Expressway running more than five years behind its original deadline. Work on three sections, spanning around 90 km, of the high-speed corridor in Gujarat is yet to start, with NHAI processing bids for two sections, including one where the last successful bidder withdrew from the project, forfeiting Rs 15 crore of bid security.The process of appointing a replacement contractor for the third section is in its final stage.The three packages in Gujarat -- package 8, 9 and 10 -- were earlier awarded to Pune-based highway developer Roadways Solutions India Infra Ltd (RSIIL), but the contracts were terminated as it failed to meet the set milestones despite getting multiple extensions, NHAI officials said.They said that for package-8 (Jujuwa to Gandewa), NHAI has received seven bids and for package 9 (Karvad to Jujuwa), there are six bids. NHAI had to go for fresh bids for package-8 after the last successful bidder, Bansal Construction Works, did not sign the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) “without quoting any reason”. TOI has learnt that officials were surprised to find that the company raised no issues and forfeited the bid security amount, which is unheard of in NHAI’s recent history.People aware of the development said RSIIL, which has been blacklisted by NHAI from bidding for projects following non-performance, has submitted a bid for package-9. Officials said that though RSIIL has moved court against NHAI’s eligibility criteria, which exclude it from bidding, Delhi High Court has green-lighted NHAI’s evaluation of the bids. The matter is scheduled to come up for hearing next week.Officials said they are confident of completing the process this month so that work can start in the next couple of months. They added that the construction work would take around two years. “These three stretches would be ready latest by December 2029. The Expressway project has faced delay due to several reasons, including Covid-19, delay in land acquisition and statutory approvals,” said one of them.People involved in the project said that apart from the three sections in Gujarat, one stretch each in Maharashtra and Rajasthan is yet to be completed. These two sections would be ready by April 2027.Govt had promised to bring down the travel time between Delhi and Mumbai by half to barely 12 hours through the expressway.

The govt’s flagship Delhi-Mumbai Expressway running more than five years behind its original deadline. Work on three sections, spanning around 90 km, of the high-speed corridor in Gujarat is yet to start.

Article Title: SC: No need for nod to prosecute govt official seeking bribe
Article Text:
The court stressed that the statutory protection is meant only to prevent persecution of officials for decisions made in discharge of their duties

NEW DELHI: In a significant ruling relating to Prevention of Corruption Act, Supreme Court has said that the shield of prior sanction from higher authorities to prosecute a public servant is not available if they are caught demanding bribes. The court stressed that the statutory protection is meant only to prevent persecution of officials for decisions made in discharge of their duties.The ruling was given by a bench of Justices SVN Bhatti and N V Anjaria while interpreting Section 17A of the Act, which was inserted in the statute in 2018 and prohibited police or investigating agencies from conducting without official approval any inquiry or investigation into alleged offences committed by public servants while discharging their duties.Dismissing an appeal by a Rajasthan police constable challenging an FIR and chargesheet against him for allegedly demanding a bribe of Rs 1.5 lakh, the bench said the Section 17A shield cannot have an omnibus application to all public servants facing prosecution for criminal offences.“The act of demanding a bribe is a pure criminal act, not connected with official functions and not relatable to or having any linkage with recommendation or decision of the appellant in his capacity as public servant,” the bench said, accepting the arguments of Rajasthan additional advocate general Sansriti Pathak.Writing the judgement, Justice Anjaria said, “In the facts and circumstances of the case, therefore, the act of the appellant does not fall within the protective umbrella of Section 17A of the Act. It could not be said that the proceedings were vitiated for want of sanction.”
Article Summary: Supreme Court said shield of prior sanction from higher authorities to prosecute a public servant is not available if they are caught demanding bribes. The court stressed that the statutory protection is meant only to prevent persecution of officials for decisions made in discharge of their duties.

Article Title: Prices of 137 cancer drugs to fall by up to 70% from November 9
Article Text:
This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients

In good news for cancer patients, prices of 137 drugs are set to be reduced by up to 70% from Nov 9, with govt capping trade margins by 30%. Drug prices regulator National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins, invoking Paragraph 19 of DPCO, 2013. Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list.The trade margin rationalisation at 30% of MRP, excluding GST, corresponds to a mark-up of 42.9% on price to stockist/price to distributor (PTS/PTD), according to the minutes of the NPPA meeting accessed by TOI. Simply put, PTS/PTD is the first point of sale of the drug.This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients, in certain cases of 10 times.The MRPs of certain drugs — including pertuzumab + trastuzumab, atezolizumab, teclistamab, inotuzumab ozogamicin and daratumumab — are up to Rs 5 lakh per vial/pack.All manufacturers will be required to inform NPPA of their revised prices within seven days of publication of the gazette notification. Manufacturers will be req-uired to display the price lists on their website and widely disseminate them to all retailers and hospitals, with the latter also required to display the revised prices on their websites prominently.The authority approved the calculation of the revised MRP based on PTS/PTD for March 2026 as the reference month.NPPA said patient assistance programme quantities may be excluded from the calculation of PTS/PTD and MRP for trade-margin capping only. These programmes, where drugs are supplied free of cost, are typically run by MNCs.As a substantial supply of anti-cancer drugs is directly made to hospitals and medical institutions, they shall be responsible for ensuring revised prices of such drugs from the date of implementation, NPPA said. State drug controllers will take necessary steps to ensure compliance by manufacturers, dealers including retailers, hospitals and medical institutions, it added.In a bid to tighten rules further, NPPA said uninterrupted availability of the covered formulations needed to be ensured. Any manufacturer intending to reduce monthly production levels would have to obtain permission.Consumers can use the Pharma Sahi Daam app and NPPA website to check revised prices of drugs, an official release said.In 2019, the MRP of 526 brands of non-scheduled anti-cancer medicines was reduced by up to 90%, NPPA said. The present exercise extends this approach to a larger set of drugs, based on the list recommended by an expert committee under Directorate General of Health Services.
Article Summary: National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) Saturday notified the 137 non- scheduled anti-cancer drugs to address the issue of excessive trade margins. Significantly, patented drugs are also included in the list. This follows a nudge by Supreme Court, flagging the huge gap between price to retailer and MRP of medicines billed to patients.

Article Title: Internet is fundamental right of all, even children: Supreme Court
Article Text:
It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.

SC: Internet’s value priceless, efficacy of curbs not proved

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Raising citizens’ right to access and use of internet to the level of fundamental right, Supreme Court has held that even children are entitled to that right and said it does not endorse imposing in the name of safety a blanket ban on children accessing internet. At the same time, it favoured restricting access to content that is inherently harmful to kids.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said that right to access and use of the internet is part of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) and Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression). The internet is “priceless” as it provides access to information and education to all in even remote areas, where it is often the only source of learning for many children. Noting that the SC had earlier refrained from expressing a definitive view on whether the right to access the internet is, by itself, a fundamental right, the bench said, “. ..we have no hesitation in saying that the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution.”SC said, “Our children, irrespective of their age enjoy the same rights, and to deny the same altogether would be as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting or freedom of speech worth expressing.”The order was passed on a public interest litigationfiled by NGO ‘Just Rights for Children Alliance’, which highlights continued lapses by intermediaries in tackling child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) despite SC’s 2024 judgment in this regard.Agreeing with its plea, SC said there has been “no progress worth the name” in the last two years.Acknowledging that there has been “a growing yet short-lived tendency across the globe in the recent past to limit the access of children below a certain age to the internet, more particularly to social media platforms,” SC said, “we too gave this our anxious consideration, and only thereafter, we decided consciously not to endorse the same”.It said the efficacy of such restrictive measures remains far from established in countries which have imposed them.“... Children do not cease to use the internet merely because the law prohibits them from doing so ... They move to other platforms and websites that are unregulated and even more unsafe,” SC said.“All that we are trying to say is that any blanket restriction on access to internet by children is nothing more than unproven measures of proven disproportionality. No jurisdiction has, so far, been able to demonstrate that children are any safer on account of such measures,” it said.It said some age-based restrictions and safeguards should exist for the safety of children online.
Article Summary: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Chandran said that right to access and use of the internet is part of Article 21 (right to life and liberty) and Article 19(1)(a) (freedom of speech and expression) The internet is “priceless” as it provides access to information and education to all in even remote areas.

NEW DELHI: The high-powered enquiry committee (HPEC) set up by SC to examine all aspects of the violent incidents that broke out during the anti-NEET paper leak protests in Delhi and beyond in July, has launched a dedicated portal for people affected by the violence, including the police personnel deployed at the protest sites, to upload their complaints and representations.The identity of the complainants/informants shall be kept confidential if they so wish.SC had constituted the HPEC to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, and at places outside Delhi, during the month of July 2026. Priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protesters, and excessive violence and destruction of property occasioned on either side.The HPEC portal ( http://hpec.nic.in) is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons. The affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints/representations making use of the formats as applicable.In addition, any person wishing to provide information/suggestion relating to the issues referred to the HPEC may also do so through the aforesaid portal, it added.Those who wish to submit the complaints, representations and other relevant material physically, can do so at the HPEC located at Shiksha Sadan, 17, Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi 110002 between 1400 hrs. and 1600 Hrs. on all working days. Submissions can also be sent by post at the above address or by email at hpec2026.enquiry@nic.in
Article Summary: SC had constituted the HPEC to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar, Delhi, and at places outside Delhi, during the month of July 2026. Priority will be given to matters pertaining to the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protesters.

Article Title: Sabarimala temple opens for Thulam month rituals; CM Satheesan offers prayers

The revered Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple was opened on Saturday for the rituals of the Thulam month, drawing numerous devotees eager to pay their respects.

Temple to open for devotees at 5 am on Sunday

Thulam rituals coincide with Mahanavami and Vijayadashami

The Sabarimala Lord Ayyappa temple opened on Saturday for the Thulam month rituals, with Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan and several other dignitaries visiting the hill shrine to offer prayers.In the presence of Tantri Kandar Brahmadathan, head priest Prasad E D opened the sanctum sanctorum and lit the ceremonial lamp. The sacred fire was then kindled in the Aazhi, located below the 18 holy steps leading to the shrine.According to news agency ANI, Devaswom Minister K Muraleedharan, Travancore Devaswom Board President K Jayakumar, Keralam State Police Chief Ravada Chandrasekhar, and MLAs Pazhakulam Madhu and C V Shanthakumar were among those, who arrived at the Sannidhanam to seek the blessings of Lord Ayyappa.Despite persistent heavy rainfall, thousands of devotees gathered at the hill shrine to offer prayers.The temple will open to devotees at 5 am on Sunday, marking the first day of the Thulam month. The selection of the new Melsanthies, or chief priests, for the Sabarimala and Malikappuram temples is also scheduled for the day through a draw of lots.The selection process for the Sabarimala Melsanthi will take place at the Sopanam at 7.30 am, following the Usha Pooja. Sabarimala Special Commissioner R Jayakrishnan and Devaswom commissioner B Sunilkumar will supervise the proceedings.The draw of lots to select the Malikappuram Melsanthi will subsequently be held at the Malikappuram temple.According to officials, this year's Thulam month rituals are particularly significant as the temple has opened during Mahanavami and Vijayadashami after several decades.The temple will close at 10 pm on October 22, following the conclusion of the Thulam month rituals.
Article Summary: Temple to open for devotees at 5 am on Sunday. Thulam month rituals coincide with Mahanavami and Vijayadashami. The selection of the new Melsanthies, or chief priests, for the Sabarimala and Malikappuram temples is also scheduled.

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu BJP on Saturday accused state ministers S Ramesh and Aadhav Arjuna of violating temple rules by facilitating the entry of an aide wearing a skull cap into the famous Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai.The BJP alleged that the incident, which took place on Saturday, went against a Madras high court order issued in January 2024 that restricts non-Hindus from proceeding beyond the temple’s flagmast unless they submit an undertaking affirming their faith in the deity and their willingness to follow Hindu customs.The party also claimed that the entry violated the temple’s dress code and religious traditions.BJP chief spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy described the incident as a “clear violation” of the court’s directions and accused the ministers of disregarding the rules governing Hindu places of worship."Temples under the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments department are places of Hindu worship, not venues for political or official disregard of agama rules, court directions, and devotee sentiments. The intervention by the HR&CE Minister to suppress objections from devotees further shows an unwillingness to uphold the very rules the department is meant to enforce," Thirupathy said on X.He demanded that both ministers issue a public apology and ensure that the High Court’s directions are followed at temples administered by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department."Such conduct undermines the legal and traditional framework protecting Hindu temples and sets a dangerous precedent. I demand that both ministers issue an immediate public apology, ensure strict compliance with the High Court order at all HR & CE temples, and take steps so that similar violations do not recur. The sanctity of places of worship must be respected without exception," he said as per news agency PTI.A video of the incident has circulated widely on social media. In the clip, a devotee can be heard questioning the HR&CE Minister over the grounds for allowing a man wearing a skull cap to enter the historic temple premises.The BJP has argued that the incident raises concerns about compliance with court directions and the rules governing access to Hindu temples.
Article Summary: BJP demands apology from ministers S Ramesh and Aadhav Arjuna. The incident took place on Saturday at the Arunachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai. The BJP alleged that the incident went against a Madras high court order issued in January 2024.

NEW DELHI: In a significant crackdown on illicit drugs network in Delhi-NCR, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) has busted two clandestine synthetic-drug manufacturing laboratories in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh, seizing a huge haul of Methamphetamine worth around Rs 50 crores, precursors and manufacturing equipment.Union home minister Amit Shah termed the operation as a 'major milestone'. "It is a remarkable example of intelligence-led enforcement and a testament to our commitment to eliminating drug cartels before December 2029," he said in a post on X.The raid, conducted under Op Crystal Hunt on Oct 16 2026 at village Jahanabad Kadalpur in Gautam Buddha Nagar, led to the recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine-containing material— encompassing crystalline, semi-crystalline, and liquid forms — alongside 10 kg of pseudoephedrine and large quantities of precursor chemicals such as acetone, toluene, and hydrochloric acid.According to officials, the seized materials are projected to yield over 56 kg of finished crystalline amphetamine. The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production.Two individuals have been arrested in connection with the operation. One suspect identified himself as Destiny Abraham Dumbiri, a Nigerian national.However, immigration checks revealed he entered India in January 2020 under the alias Francis Kalokoh using a tourist visa that expired in December of that year, underscoring the sophisticated tactics used by traffickers to evade law enforcement.The second accused, Ms Lallawmzuali, alias Olivia Lalchawimawii, a resident of Mizoram, was out on bail following an earlier arrest in March 2026 by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence in Goa for allegedly possessing a commercial quantity of heroin.This latest operation builds upon the NCB's ongoing efforts to dismantle organized cartels, echoing a previous October 2024 raid in the Kasna Industrial Area that exposed suspected ties to the Mexican cartel Cártel de Jalisco Nueva Generación.Investigators are tracing the financial trails, chemical procurement channels, and broader distribution networks associated with the arrested pair to uncover further interstate and international links.Beyond the direct threat of narcotics, authorities emphasized the severe environmental and public health hazards posed by such hidden facilities, noting that the untreated discharge of chemical waste severely contaminates local soil, drainage systems, and water bodies.The NCB has issued a strong public appeal urging landlords, property dealers, housing societies, and Resident Welfare Associations to remain vigilant. "Citizens are encouraged to report suspicious indicators such as unusual chemical odors, unexplained storage of drums, or heavy lab equipment to the National Narcotics Helpline MANAS at 1933, reinforcing the nation's collective stride toward a Nasha Mukt Bharat," the NCB said.
Article Summary: The premises were heavily equipped with large-capacity heating mantles, glass reaction vessels, filtration machinery, and laboratory apparatus tailored for mass production. The raid led to the recovery of nearly 380 kg of amphetamine- containing material, alongside 10 kg of pseudoephedrine and large quantities of precursor chemicals.
