NEW DELHI: An enquiry committee constituted by the Supreme Court launched a complaint portal on Saturday for individuals and police personnel affected by violence during July protests at Jantar Mantar, in and around Delhi.The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) has launched the portal for affected individuals to upload their complaints/representations, as applicable, regarding the committed violence.Ministry of home affairs informed that the portal has been designed to keep the complainant’s identity confidential, if they desire.“The Portal is designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons”, home ministry said in a statement.The committee would prioritise incidents that involved the use of pellet guns, targeted violence and harassment of female protestors, and excessive violence and destruction of property, the ministry said.Additionally, HPEC would examine all issues mentioned in paragraphs 12 and 13 of the Supreme Court’s order dated August 18, 2026, and paragraph 5(i) of the order dated September 10, 2026.“Apart from the above, any person wishing to provide information/suggestion relating to the issues referred to the HPEC under the Orders dated 18 August 2026 and 10 September 2026 may also do so through the aforesaid portal,” the ministry said.Complaints, representations and other relevant material can also be submitted in person at the HPEC office at Shiksha Sadan, 17, Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi 110002, between 2 pm and 4 pm on all working days.Submissions may also be sent by post to the same address or via email.
Article Summary: The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC) has launched the portal for affected individuals to upload their complaints/representations. The portal has been designed to keep the complainant’s identity confidential, if they desire. The committee would prioritise incidents that involved the use of pellet guns and targeted violence.

Article Title: Man killed, four injured in suspected militant attack on Kuki village in Manipur
Article Text:
Violence has been escalating in Manipur

A 36-year old man was killed and four others injured after suspected militants attacked Chassad village in Manipur's Kamjong district on Saturday, triggering an exchange of fire between the assailants and a local armed group, police said.Several rounds were fired at the Kuki village around 2.30 pm, and the gunfight was continuing in the evening, a senior police officer said, according to PTI."Village head Thangjahou Haokip (48), and four others - Khailun Haokip, Seikhohou, Hegin Haokip and Seipao Haokip - were injured after the suspected militants attacked the village. All the injured were taken to a hospital where Seikhohou succumbed to his injuries," the officer said."The gunfight is still underway in the evening," the officer added.The Committee on Tribal Unity condemned the attack and urged the state government to deploy central forces in the area.The latest violence comes amid broader reported cases of violence. The escalating clashes between Kuki-Zo and Naga communities, which have claimed more than 50 lives since February, with homes and shops torched and civilians caught in attacks across several districts.Last week, nine people, including six Nagas, two Kukis and a Gorkha farmer, were killed in a series of attacks across three districts in a 12-hour period. The violence included an attack on Chassad village and gunfights in Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts. Houses and shops were also set on fire, prompting prohibitory orders in Kamjong and a shutdown call on National Highway 202.The situation remained tense on Thursday, when a Kuki-Zo woman, Hatneikim Haokip, was killed and her husband injured in an alleged ambush by suspected Naga militants on the road between Phaikoh and Aishu in Kamjong district. Two other people travelling with them were reported missing. The woman was reportedly travelling with the group to buy essential commodities.The violence has also affected Kamjong, Ukhrul, Kangpokpi, Tamenglong, Noney and other districts, raising concerns over security in the state and along the India-Myanmar border.
Article Summary: A 36-year old man was killed and four others injured after suspected militants attacked Chassad village in Manipur's Kamjong district on Saturday. The Committee on Tribal Unity condemned the attack and urged the state government to deploy central forces in the area.
